questions.text: What are you trying to do with business data?

options.text: Find out whether the records from my business have valuable stuff worth licensing.
Get another estimate for records I can license and am already shopping around.
Bring several businesses, datasets, or companies I can introduce your way.
Acquire full company datasets for our downstream buyers, not license my own records.
I'm not sure which of these describes my situation.

questions.text: What would be the most useful next step?

options.text: Review the depth and breadth of our archive and explain whether it fits.
Compare the offer on the table with a fair fee and terms.
Work out which of several opportunities to pursue without repeating the same work.
Receive an actionable company inventory and seller asking price for our buyers to evaluate.
I'm still unsure what needs to happen next.

questions.text: What is your role in getting the data into a deal?

options.text: I own or represent one business whose records could be licensed; we haven't received an offer.
I represent the supplier and am comparing an offer or licensing services.
I represent several businesses or introduce companies through a referral or affiliate relationship.
I evaluate or acquire other companies' datasets for downstream buyers.
My role or permission to proceed still needs to be worked out.

questions.text: What is already in place for the next step?

options.text: One business archive; I still need a fit review before seeking an offer.
An offer or licensing terms from another provider that I want to compare.
Several company opportunities, data rooms, intake forms, or introductions to review.
Our buyers' requirements; we need qualified suppliers and an actionable inventory.
None of these is clear yet.

questions.text: What would help you decide whether your archive has valuable stuff worth licensing?

options.text: Review the years of data and the systems our business used.
Check the typical minimum against our staff history, not just today's team.
Get the introduction or missing invitation so I can take the next steps.
Actually, I already have an offer and want another estimate.
I'm still unsure.

questions.text: Where are you with the review or introduction?

options.text: I haven't started; I need to know where to begin.
I've described the archive and am waiting for a fit review.
I'm waiting for the introduction or the actual inventory invitation.
I've submitted the inventory and am following up on next steps.
Actually, I'm comparing an offer rather than starting a review.

questions.text: What do you need to compare before choosing an offer?

options.text: The license fee for our records.
Exclusive versus non-exclusive rights in the supplier offer.
When we would be paid and what our offer requires us to deliver.
Another estimate and a comparable manifest or inventory.
Actually, I don't have an offer; I need to know whether our archive fits.

questions.text: How much time do you have to compare the offer?

options.text: The offer on the table expires tomorrow, or has another firm deadline.
I have an offer, but no firm decision date has been set.
We're shopping it around and still discussing a fair fee and terms.
Actually, I haven't received an offer yet.

questions.text: Which different opportunities are you bringing our way?

options.text: Several datasets from businesses I own or represent.
Companies I can introduce through a referral or affiliate relationship.
Several data rooms and intake forms I've already shared.
Actually, this is one business archive, not several opportunities.
Actually, we're acquiring datasets for buyers, not supplying or referring them.

questions.text: What would help you avoid wasting time or opportunities?

options.text: Review each company's inventory separately so we know which opportunities fit.
Confirm what is missing from the data rooms or intake forms I've already shared.
Explain how the affiliate or referral relationship works before I introduce more companies.
Check the coverage dates and team continuity of several datasets before we do more work.
Actually, I need an estimate against one existing supplier offer.

questions.text: What makes an opportunity actionable for your team?

options.text: Company name, inventory, and the seller's asking price for our buyers to evaluate.
A full corpus with the years of data and systems clearly described.
A seller with authority to sign, plus clear delivery and acceptance conditions.
Actually, I introduce companies; I don't acquire their data for buyers.
Actually, I want to license the records from my own business.

questions.text: What has to be checked before you can accept a dataset?

options.text: The seller's rights and authority, so the opportunity can move without more approval rounds.
Years of operating data, team continuity, and systems used.
The full corpus against our buyers' requirements, not just a list of company names.
The agreed delivery and acceptance conditions before payment can be approved.
Our acceptance requirements still need to be worked out.

questions.text: In your own words, what is holding up your next steps?
What would make this worth your time?
questions.supporting_text: Describe the result you want and any deadline, license terms, or data requirements that matter.
